extracted.intended_audience: Vanity Fair readers and the general public interested in fashion, celebrity culture, and Met Gala coverage
extracted.subtask_description: Implicit evaluative criteria used by Vanity Fair / guests to judge Met Gala and afterparty looks — what makes someone stand out as 'best dressed' at the event. Focus is on thematic commitment, theatricality, craftsmanship, symbolism, and social reaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lean into the theme
rubrics_metrics.description: “people who really leaned into the theme.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Willa Bennett said she most appreciated people who 'really leaned into the theme,' citing Chase Infiniti and Emma Chamberlain as standout examples. Implies favoring looks that overtly respond to the event's theme rather than safe or generic outfits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take the theme seriously / thematic commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Guests were 'praising those who took this year’s theme, “fashion is art”, seriously.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of serious commitment include highly conceptual or art-referential ensembles such as Madonna recreating an obscure surrealist painting, Heidi Klum as a 'living sculpture,' and Bad Bunny using prosthetics to age himself—looks that explicitly engage the 'fashion is art' conceit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theatricality and extremity
rubrics_metrics.description: Emphasis on 'the most extreme looks from the carpet uptown' and theatrical, showy choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited examples: Heidi Klum's stone 'living sculpture,' Madonna's pirate-ship headpiece with a six-piece veil, and Bad Bunny's extensive prosthetics. Rewards bold, dramatic, and attention-grabbing presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation and craftsmanship
rubrics_metrics.description: “All this energy, all this prep work and you’re trying to be present.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jeremy Pope described the level of preparation required for the gala, noting archival and elaborately beaded garments (e.g., Vivienne Westwood) — this favors technically accomplished, meticulously prepared looks that show evident labor and craft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symbolism and personal narrative
rubrics_metrics.description: Garments that convey personal meaning or complex symbolism — e.g., Pope's piece with 'red slashes on the back that resemble a bleeding body' representing 'the nuance of me as a Black man.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Looks that embody or communicate identity, lived experience, or layered concepts are highlighted; judges/readers value when outfit elements function as narrative or social commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social validation and memorability
rubrics_metrics.description: Guest reactions and social-media sharing shape judgments: attendees 'were excitedly sharing photos' and named moments like bumping into Rihanna and A$AP Rocky as highlights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer recognition, celebrity interactions, and viral shareability contribute to a look's status as 'best dressed' — memorable moments and social buzz are part of the evaluative calculus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artistic reinvention / inventive references
rubrics_metrics.description: Reimagining or directly referencing art and art-historical sources (e.g., Madonna's surrealist painting recreation) is prized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outfits that cleverly reinterpret artwork or art movements—bringing high-concept references into wearable form—are considered strong responses to a 'fashion is art' brief.
